papers.title_en: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.authors: Zhangyang Peng, Jingze Shi, Tongyi Zhang, Yuyu Luo
papers.evidence: 面向表格基础模型的生成器状态监督
papers.tldr: 表格基础模型预训练常用采样硬查询标签，带来可避免的采样波动。GIST观察到生成器中间状态能揭示标签不确定性，据此对条件标签分布上的查询损失做平均，并联合设计任务生成与查询监督。该方法保持总体目标且不增大梯度协方差。在三个架构、TabArena和TALENT上，GIST不改变架构或推理即提升平均排名，并在成对数据集比较中胜出62.1%。表明生成器状态可作为更稳定监督信号。
papers.abstract_en: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) based on prior-data fitted networks typically use sampled hard query labels, leaving avoidable sampling variability in pretraining. A key observation is that intermediate generator states can reveal label uncertainty beyond a sampled outcome. We propose Generator-state-Informed Supervision for TFMs (GIST), which uses these states to average query losses over conditional label distributions. GIST jointly designs task generation and query supervision, using entropy-calibrated encodings to obtain tractable, input-consistent targets on supported label-dependent branches. We show that this averaging preserves the population objective and yields no larger gradient covariance at fixed parameters within each generating distribution. Under matched pretraining schedules, GIST improves mean rank across three architectures on both TabArena and TALENT without changing architecture or inference. Across these benchmarks and architectures, GIST wins 62.1% of paired dataset-level comparisons against the corresponding hard-label controls.

papers.title_en: Tabular Foundation Models Are Effectively Shallow
papers.evidence: 表格基础模型架构简化
papers.tldr: 表格基础模型（TFMs）免训练但多Transformer块堆叠导致高算力与显存开销，而GBDT在CPU上仍具竞争力。作者提出闭式、无标签的仿射转换器，可替换连续窗口内最多96%的块，其余不变。在8个前沿TFMs与171个分类数据集上，替换半数块的中位AUROC损失至多0.002，半深度TabFM仍优于全深度TFMs和调优GBDT。移除深度最多省1.5B参数、GPU推理快6倍，单块TabPFN-3缓存查询快2.4倍且省6倍显存。
papers.abstract_en: In-context-learning Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) are uniquely suited to scenarios with limited resources or privacy constraints, as they solve new tasks without additional training. However, their architecture consists of multiple transformer blocks, resulting in high computational and memory footprints. Meanwhile, traditional alternatives like Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees (GBDTs) remain highly competitive and run efficiently on CPUs, suggesting that tabular tasks may not inherently require deep architectures. This contrast raises a fundamental question: can TFMs be simplified by removing architectural redundancies without sacrificing performance? To answer this, we introduce a closed-form, label-free affine translator that replaces a contiguous window of up to 96% of the blocks, leaving the rest unchanged. Evaluating eight frontier TFMs on 171 classification datasets, we reveal that tabular transformers are vastly overparameterized: replacing half of a model's blocks costs at most $0.002$ median AUROC across all architectures, with the half-depth TabFM still outperforming every other full-depth TFMs and tuned GBDTs. Furthermore, different model families are overparameterized in different ways: TabPFN-3 relies on its encoders, maintaining performance regardless of which single block is retained. Other single-axis models spread computation thinly, needing only their first block, while dual-axis models concentrate it in one critical block. Ultimately, removing depth saves up to 1.5B parameters, speeds up GPU inference by up to $6\times$ at a median cost of $0.03$ AUROC, while a single-block TabPFN-3 serves cached queries $2.4\times$ faster using $6\times$ less memory at negligible cost.

papers.title_en: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
papers.authors: Tianqi Zhao, Jia Guo, Yan Shuo Tan, Qiong Zhang
papers.evidence: 评估表格基础模型的基准
papers.tldr: 表格基础模型（TFM）预测性能强，但其后验预测分布（PPD）的可靠性研究不足。本文从点预测、分布质量、边际与子组校准、区间效率评估可靠性，并提出覆盖分类与回归的TabReliBench基准。结果显示，模型排名随基准和指标变化；回归模型边际覆盖近名义且区间窄，但边际好不代表条件覆盖有效。分类难度常伴随校准差，回归性能不能可靠指示校准，集成与共形后处理也难稳定改善校准，可靠选型需多维评估。
papers.abstract_en: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are increasingly popular for their strong predictive performance. Many also provide posterior predictive distributions (PPDs), whose reliability remains less studied. We assess reliability through point prediction, distributional quality, marginal and subgroup calibration, and interval efficiency. We then introduce TabReliBench, a large classification and regression benchmark for these comparisons and dataset-level analyses. We find that TFMs' rankings change between TabArena and our benchmark and across reliability metrics. Regression TFMs usually achieve near-nominal marginal coverage and retain narrow intervals, but this favorable marginal behavior does not imply valid conditional coverage. Dataset-level analyses show that classification difficulty often accompanies poor calibration, whereas regression predictive performance is not a reliable indicator of calibration. Ensembling improves predictive performance but does not consistently improve calibration of PPDs; TFMs also benefit little from conformal post-processing, which does not reliably resolve subgroup gaps. Reliable TFM selection therefore requires multidimensional evaluation beyond aggregate rankings. Code is available at https://github.com/Tianqi-Zhao/TabReliBench.

papers.title_en: TabMF: Learning Dataset Representations with Tabular Foundation Models
papers.authors: Rafiq Kamel, Nicolas Atienza, Aziz Fouché, Nicola Cancedda, Josif Grabocka
papers.evidence: 将表格基础模型用作数据集编码器
papers.tldr: 监督数据集表示可用于数据集检索与分布偏移监控，但现有方法依赖手工元特征或专用编码器。TabMF将预训练表格基础模型改造成数据集编码器，加入架构感知的数据集级读出，并用合成监督数据集的随机视图做对比式后训练。在TabICLv2与TabPFN-2.5上实例化后，于未见真实数据集的六项任务中，两个编码器取得最强综合表现，检索、紧凑基准构建和分布偏移严重度评估尤其突出，表明预测预训练已蕴含数据集级结构。
papers.abstract_en: Representations of supervised datasets support higher-level machine-learning tasks such as dataset retrieval and distribution-shift monitoring. However, existing approaches typically rely either on hand-crafted meta-features or on dataset encoders trained specifically for representation learning. We introduce TabMF, a framework that repurposes pretrained tabular foundation models (TFMs) as encoders of supervised datasets. TabMF equips a predictive TFM with an architecture-aware dataset-level readout and adapts the model end-to-end using contrastive post-training on stochastic views of synthetic supervised datasets. We instantiate TabMF on TabICLv2 and TabPFN-2.5 and evaluate the resulting representations across six tasks on unseen real datasets. Simple frozen TFM readouts yield competitive representations, indicating that predictive pretraining already induces substantial dataset-level structure. The two TabMF encoders obtain the strongest aggregate performance among the evaluated learned and classical dataset representations, with particularly strong results in dataset retrieval, compact benchmark construction, and distribution-shift severity assessment.
